message: **The pre-header streaming budget's doc now says what "the next candidate" depends on.** `resilience.pre_header_timeout_ms` bounds connect through the provider's response headers and hands the request on when it elapses, and the handoff goes to whatever the origin's routing strategy makes next. `fallback_chain`, which is what the documented example uses, names a declared successor and the request reaches it. A strategy that spreads requests rather than ordering them, `round_robin` among them, has no successor to hand it to: the elapse still bounds the attempt and is still counted on `sbproxy_ai_failovers_total{reason="pre_header_timeout"}`, but the caller gets the refusal rather than the sibling. Both behaviors were measured against one binary with the same budget and the same upstreams, differing only in the strategy, in `e2e/tests/sota_gateway_integration.rs`. No code changed; the page now states the pairing instead of leaving it to be inferred from the example. See [docs/ai-llm-aware-resilience.md](docs/ai-llm-aware-resilience.md#pre-header-streaming-budget).
